verdict.rationale: GrowthBook ships no documented one-click 'export everything' feature, but its own capabilities support leaving with your data. It is open source and self-hostable, so the data sits on your own infrastructure. It is warehouse-native, so event and metric data stay in your warehouse. A full REST API returns experiment results for your own reporting, and the OpenFeature provider means switching vendors only requires changing the bootstrap. Missing for 10: a documented bulk export of all configuration (flags, experiments, metrics) in open formats, documented export file formats, hands-on evidence of a complete export-and-migrate.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Switching from or to GrowthBook only requires changing the provider bootstrap, not a single flag call.
Get results for an experiment (`GET /v1/experiments/{id}/results`) to pull the latest analysis into your own reporting.
GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.
Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
Warehouse Native. Query 11 data sources including BigQuery, Snowflake, and Databricks.
